help.settings: carryCapacity is the most weight a person can carry. walkSpeed is in metres per second. worldSize is how wide the square world is in metres (100 makes it 100 m x 100 m, with the clearing in the middle); it can be 40 to 300, and the bigger it is the more your phone has to draw. needsSpeed is 1 for real time; set it higher to test, for example 60 makes an hour of hunger and thirst pass in a minute. autoName fills in a name from testNames on the Make your person screen (handy while testing; set it to false for the real game). respawnMinutes is how often (online) the world adds one stick and one stone, if there are fewer on the ground than startInWorld: sticks under trees, stones by boulders. maxPlaying is how many people can play at once (20 for now, to stay inside Cloudflare's free plan); anyone else waits in line on the main menu and joins by themselves when a spot opens. Run tools/worlds.py test-build after changing it. worldTimeZone is the one clock the whole world runs on (date, time, day and night), the same for every player: Australia/Darwin for the Oceania world. craftSearchFrom: Craft shows a search box once you know this many recipes.
help.items: To add an item, copy one of the items above, give it a new id (lower case, no spaces) and set its name, plural, weight and look. It then shows up by itself in the Inventory, in Craft (if a recipe makes it) and in the admin's Add list, with a picture drawn from its look. Shapes and their looks: rod (length, thickness, colour, twig), rock (size, colour), ball (size, colour, leaf: a colour or false), axe (length, thickness, colour, head, lashing), log (length, radius, colour, end), knife (length, thickness, colour, blade, lashing), coil (size, colour), campfire (size, colour, stone, ash), box (width, height, depth, colour). An unknown shape is drawn as a rock. eat is what eating one gives (a berry gives hunger 10), which adds an Eat button in the inventory. tool: {"uses": 20} makes it a tool that wears out after that many uses (a wear bar in the inventory); a tool shows in your hand only while you use it (chopping, cutting). startInWorld is how many lie around when the world starts (0 for things you can only make), and startNear is how many of those start close to where you appear. After changing items, run python3 tools/worlds.py test-build so the server knows about them. about (optional) is a short line shown when you tap it in the Inventory; without it, the about of the recipe that makes it is used. startInWorld: how many lie about the world; while there are fewer, one more turns up every settings.respawnMinutes, at a spot by spawnsNear (trees or boulders). A new item with startInWorld and spawnsNear starts turning up by itself, no reset needed (run tools/worlds.py test-build).
help.recipes: To add a recipe, put it in the recipes list like this: {"id": "stone-axe", "name": "Stone axe", "needs": {"stick": 2, "stone": 3}, "makes": {"stone-axe": 1}, "about": "Chops trees"}. Every item in needs and makes must exist in items. Recipes show up in the Craft sheet (the hammer button) automatically. about is a short line on the recipe card (optional). The server checks crafting too, so run python3 tools/worlds.py test-build after changing recipes. near (optional) is a placeable id, like campfire: the recipe can then only be made close to a built one (a fire has to be lit), Craft shows a 'By a lit campfire' chip, and it's listed in that thing's tap menu under its craftLabel (Cook). Use it for cooking. A recipe shows in Craft once you've had all but one of the things it needs (at least one), so players discover recipes as they find new things. group (optional) puts it under a button in Craft (Tools, Food, Building, Clothes, Materials); without it tools go under Tools, food under Food, things you place under Building and the rest under Materials.
help.looks: Each list here is a set of choices on the Make your person screen. Add an entry to add a choice.
help.stats: Stats run in real time. Every stat goes from 0 to 100. perHour is how much it changes each real hour, and whileAsleep is used instead while sleeping. lowAt shows the warning (the ring pulses red, and under 10 it flashes). atZero is what happens to other stats each hour while this one is empty. Health heals (4 an hour, 8 asleep, so about a day to full) when nothing is empty, and the person dies when health reaches 0. fullLabel is shown when you try to eat or drink but don't need to. Hunger lasts about a day (a berry fills 10), thirst about 16 hours awake (a drink fills 15), Rest about 16 hours awake and 8 asleep (whileAsleepAtNight: faster at night, about 6 hours). With no water you die in about 3 days, with no food in about a week. collapseAtZero (Rest): when it runs out your person collapses asleep where they stand and can't be woken until it's back to wakeAt (25). Energy is not deadly. icon: heart, food, drop, moon or bolt. The server uses the same numbers (copied by tools/worlds.py).
help.sources: Things in the world you can use, matched by name ("Pond", "Berry bush"). action is the button in the tap menu, like "Drink". gives adds to stats each time (one drink at the pond gives 15 thirst). harvest is what one pick puts in your inventory (1 berry), holds is how many a full bush has (up to 15), and regrowHours is how long a picked-bare bush takes to grow them all back; picked berries grow back one at a time. seconds is how long it takes. pose is kneel, pick or bend. tool and toolHarvest: with that tool you get toolHarvest per pick instead (a knife picks 2 berries), and the tool wears.
help.defaultLook: How a new person starts on the Make your person screen.
help.daylight: Day and night follow the player's real local time. Each entry is how the world looks at that hour, and the game blends between them. sky is the haze colour, skyLight and groundLight light things from above and below, brightness is how strong that is, sun is the sun or moon colour, sunStrength how strong, sunHeight its angle in degrees.
help.version: version is the game version and build counts the test copies of that version (start build at 1 for each new version, count up for each test copy). Both only need changing here.
help.server: server is the address of the online world. The test link joins the test world and the release joins the live world. Leave it empty to play offline.
help.chatFilter: Words kept out of speech bubbles (shown as stars) and names (pick another). anywhere: caught even inside a longer word. words: only caught as a whole word (so 'class' is fine), plus endings like s, ed, ing. phrases: caught as a run of words. Numbers and symbols standing in for letters (sh1t, @ss) are caught too. The server gets a copy: tools/worlds.py test-build copies it to server/words.json. names: extra words only kept out of names, so nobody can pretend to be the admin.
help.away: How a person looks after themselves while their player is away (the server does this). near: 'pond' keeps them strolling round the main pond (anything else: round where you left them). wanderMin and wanderMax: how far in metres from there they stroll. strollSpeed in metres per second. They eat what they carry when hunger is under eatBelow, go for berries if they have none, and drink at the pond when thirst is under drinkBelow. After sleepAfterHours away they lie down asleep: hunger and thirst keep dropping slowly (the asleep rates) but stop at asleepFloor, so they can't die; after goneAfterDays asleep (3 days away in all) they leave the world and their things stay where they slept. A grave marks where someone died for graveHours. idleMinutes: if you're in the game but don't touch anything for this long, your person goes on autopilot and does the same, until you tap. sleepBelow: someone on autopilot or away lies down to sleep when Rest is under this, and gets up when it's full. At night (see night) they go to sleep until morning. comeBackSeconds: for this long after a player's connection goes, their person stays right where they are, so a short break in the connection changes nothing (the game carries on from where it was). With a claim (see claims) they stay within it instead of by the pond, keep its fire fed from their bag, and still walk to the pond to drink.
help.berryBushes: extra: how many more berry bushes grow out in the wider world, besides the ones by the start. seed: their own random numbers, so they're in the same places on every phone (change it to move them all).
help.devlog: What's new, shown in the Menu. Newest first: version, date and a short list of changes, written for players.
help.energyCosts: Stamina (the yellow ring, id energy) is short-term: every task takes these amounts and walking takes walkPerMetre for each metre. It comes back by itself quickly (perHour in its need: 600 an hour, so empty to full in about 10 minutes; whileAsleep 1500 when sleeping, whileSitting 2400 when sitting by a fire). Below slowBelow (20) your person is out of breath: walking and tasks take slowBy (1.5) times as long. It never stops you and it's not deadly. The server uses the same numbers.
help.chopping: Chopping with a tool (tool: the item you need). tree: chopping a standing tree (seconds, and what falls: gives); it leaves a stump that grows back into a tree after regrowDays real days. stump: digging out a stump (then the tree is gone for good). log: chopping a log (an item) into sticks. Each chop wears the tool by one use, and takes energyCosts.chop energy. The server uses the same rules.
help.plants: Plants you cut, like tall grass. Each kind is laid out by itself: count clumps (nearStart of them near the start), on its own random numbers (seed) so nothing else moves. action is the tap menu button, verb what shows while doing it. gives goes into your inventory each cut. seconds is how long by hand, toolSeconds with the tool (each use wears the tool). regrowHours [lo, hi]: a cut clump grows back at a random time in between. look: blades per clump, height, colour and tips (the seed heads). Run tools/worlds.py test-build after changing plants.
help.regions: The worlds (regions) on the main menu, under Play. Each is its own world on its own clock (timeZone). open: false shows it as Coming soon; tapping it shows this world's view at that region's time of day. For now only one world exists, so only one region can be open, and its timeZone should match settings.worldTimeZone.
help.night: Night in the world's clock (settings.worldTimeZone), from the hour 'from' to the hour 'to'. Sleeping at night fills Rest at whileAsleepAtNight instead of whileAsleep. People away or on autopilot go to sleep when night starts and get up in the morning. The server uses the same numbers.
help.placeables: Things you place in the world and build, like the campfire. An item with places (the id of an entry here) gets a Place button in the Inventory: you pick a spot, your person puts it down as an unbuilt site, then builds it (buildSeconds; buildVerb shows while building). solid is how big it is for walking round (metres). fire makes it a fire you can light and put out: fuel is the item you add (sticks), secondsEach is how long one burns (300 = 5 minutes), otherFuels are more items it burns with their seconds each (log: 1800), maxHours is the most it holds in hours of burning (72 = 3 days, so a claim's fire can last the 3-day away timer; without maxHours, maxFuel counts it in fuel items), lightSeconds how long lighting takes. It only burns while lit, keeps burning while players are away, and goes out by itself when the fuel runs out. seats: people can sit round it (count places, distance metres from the middle). Sitting is a task with no set time: your person sits until you stand up, do something else or the fire goes out, and keeps sitting while you're away. Run tools/worlds.py test-build after changing placeables. craftLabel names the tap menu list of recipes made there (recipes with near), like Cook.
help.mining: Mining with a tool (tool: the item you need, the stone pickaxe). rock: breaking a small rock (seconds, and what falls: gives); the rock is then gone, but one broken rock comes back by a boulder every rockBackHours. boulder: mining a boulder; gives can be a range like [3, 5]. A mined boulder stays (it can't be removed) and can be mined again after regrowDays real days (the same as trees). Each hit wears the tool by one use and takes energyCosts.chop energy. The server uses the same rules.
help.liveSettings: Numbers the admin can change live from the Admin panel (Settings tab) without a new build. Each one's id is wired up in code (server/src/live.js and test/game/admin.js); name, group, unit, min, max and step are just how it shows. The normal value still comes from the rest of this file (settings, chopping, mining, sources, stats); a live change wins until the admin taps Reset.
help.testNames: Only for testing: with settings.autoName on, Make your person fills in a random name from this list. autoName is off in the real game, so players type their own name (the checks in tools/tests switch it on for themselves).
help.bodyShapes: The body builds on Make your person (slim, average and so on): how much wider or taller each part of the body is drawn. Add one by copying an entry; it shows up as a choice by itself.
help.claims: Claims (0.3.0): your first campfire becomes your claim when you light it: radius metres round it, yours only while the fire burns (once it's out the land is free and anyone can take the cold fire apart). One claim each. Claims can't overlap and can't reach into the free area round the main pond (spawnRadius metres from the pond's middle; the pond itself is about 6 m across from its middle). Inside someone else's claim others can only walk through. placeable: the kind that claims. ringShowsWithin: how near you have to be to see a claim's faint ring. Run tools/worlds.py test-build after changing it.

notes: If something ever goes badly wrong, the world can now be put back to how it was a little earlier, so your progress is safer.
Behind the scenes: the server keeps track of who's online much more cheaply, so the world copes with far more people.
Busy worlds run more smoothly: only the people near you are drawn in full, and fewer of them on the lower graphics settings.
If something goes wrong, the game keeps going and quietly lets us know, instead of freezing.
Behind the scenes: the world saves less often for people who are away, so it copes with lots more people.
Claims: light your first campfire and the land 10 m round it becomes your claim, for as long as the fire burns. A faint ring shows its edge.
Inside someone else's claim you can walk through, but you can't build, pick things up, chop, mine, pick berries, cut grass or use their fire.
Logs now burn for 8 hours, and a campfire holds up to 3 days of fuel. Sticks still burn for 5 minutes each.
If your fire goes out, your claim is gone and anyone can take the cold fire apart. You get one claim, and the land round the pond can't be claimed.
While you're away your person stays near their claim, keeps its fire going with sticks and logs from their bag, and walks to the pond for water.
Make your person: ages 13 to 90, and you type your own name.
The Menu now has What's new, Settings and Feedback, so you don't have to leave the world for them.
A short break in your connection no longer loses what you were doing: your person waits for you, and what you finished is sent when you're back.
Fair play: the world now checks you're next to what you pick up, chop, mine or drink from.
Tidier wording (Pick berries, Too heavy), and lots of sticks and stones on the ground no longer slow phones down.
Fixed: the note when placing a campfire no longer squashes into a narrow column on some phones.
The stone pickaxe works now. Tap a rock and Break rock (about 10 s) to get 5 stones. The rock is gone, but broken rocks slowly come back beside boulders.
Tap a boulder and Mine boulder (about 15 s) for 3 to 5 stones. Boulders stay for good; a mined one looks worn down and can be mined again after 3 days, like a tree stump growing back.
Tap a mined boulder to see how long until you can mine it again.
Sit by campfire is one tap now, with no time to pick. Your person sits until you tap Stand up, give them something else to do, or the fire goes out.
New: the stone pickaxe, made from 2 sticks, 3 stones and 1 twine. What it's for is coming soon.
Giving your person a task while they're sitting by the fire makes them stand up and do it.
The stone knife and stone pickaxe have new looks to match the stone axe: shaped stone heads, a grip at the end and twine lashing.
The old tree stumps and fallen logs are gone from the world. Stumps now only come from trees that have been chopped down, and they grow back into trees.
Tap a tree stump to see how long until it grows back into a tree.
Recipes are found as you go: one shows in Craft once you've had all but one of the things it needs, and Craft says how many are still to find.
Craft has buttons for Tools, Food and Building, and a search box once you know lots of recipes.
Tap a recipe's name to see more about it.
You can drop any tool, including the one you're using.
Campfires can be packed up into your inventory or taken apart once they're out. Only the person who built one can do that, and once a fire has been lit, taking it apart gives back just the stones.
Each tool keeps its own wear, and a worn tool stays worn when you drop it and pick it up again (it used to come back as new). Tap one on the ground to see its uses left.
New inventory: your things are tiles in a grid, and each tool gets its own. Tap one to see what it is and what you can do with it, and tap it again to hide that.
Craft with, on an item in your inventory, shows only the recipes that use it.
Craft shows what you can make right now first.
Tidier campfire menu: the time left shows at the top, Add fuel has its own list, and Inspect and Walk here sit small along the bottom (the same in every tap menu).
Sticks and stones turn up on the ground every 5 minutes (was 10), up to the usual amount, so it never gets cluttered.
The sticks in a campfire look full again at about 50 minutes of fuel.
New weights: logs 5 (was 10), campfires 12 (was 17), twine, berries and the stone knife 1 each.
Tools last longer: the stone knife 20 uses (was 10), the stone axe 30 (was 20).
Logs burn on a campfire: 30 minutes each (a stick is 5). A fire now holds up to 2 hours of fuel.
Chopping a log into sticks gives 5 sticks (was 4).
Stamina comes back faster: full again in about 10 minutes (was 15).
Sitting by a campfire fills Stamina in about 2 to 3 minutes, and sleeping in about 4.
Chopping takes a bit less Stamina (10, was 15).
A campfire now takes 4 stones too (1 log, 3 sticks and 4 stones), for the ring round the fire.
Sitting by the fire, your feet stay out of the flames (seats are a bit further back).
Your hands are empty unless you're using a tool: the axe comes out to chop and the knife to cut, then they're put away.
On the main menu, worlds that aren't open yet look fresh and untouched: every tree standing, nothing on the ground and nobody there.
Campfires! Craft one from 1 log and 3 sticks (the hammer button).
Place it from your Inventory: tap the ground to pick a spot, then Place. Your person puts it down and builds it.
Tap a campfire to add sticks, light it, put it out or check how much fuel is left. Each stick burns for 5 minutes and it holds up to 10.
The fire keeps burning while you're away and goes out by itself when the sticks run out.
Sit by a lit campfire for 5 minutes up to an hour. Your person keeps sitting even if you close the game, and others can sit round it too.
You can now be away for 3 days before your person leaves the world (was 2).
After the first day away your person sleeps on the ground. Hunger and thirst still drop slowly, but stop at 10%, so you come back hungry and thirsty but alive.
Sleeping at night (8 pm to 6 am) fills Rest faster: about 6 hours instead of 8.
People away or on autopilot now go to bed when it gets dark and get up in the morning.
Ageing: your person gets a year older on their birthday each real year, from the day you made them.
World picker: each world shows how many people are in it, and a world that's coming soon shows empty.
Fixed people getting stuck in the pond: you can always wade out, and nobody comes back or appears standing in the water.
Twine looks like twine now: a coil of thin cord, tied across, with a loose end.
New home: the game is now at pocketlife.pages.dev. The old address sends you there and you keep your person.
The main menu has a world picker under Play: Oceania (Darwin time) is open now, with Europe and Americas coming soon. Tap one to see the world at that time of day.
People away from the game no longer walk through trees or get stuck: they keep to a route round things and keep up with where they're meant to be.
A big clean-up behind the scenes so lots of new things can be added quickly. Nothing about how the game plays has changed.
One clock for the whole world: it runs on Darwin time for everyone, so day and night are the same for all players (other regions can come later).
Energy is now short-term stamina: it drains as you work and walk and comes back in about 15 minutes. When it's low you slow down instead of stopping.
Health heals faster when you're fed, watered and rested: about a day from low to full, quicker asleep.
New: tall grass. Cut it for twine (6 s by hand, 2 s with a knife); it grows back in 1 to 4 hours.
New: Stone knife (1 stick, 1 stone, 1 twine). It cuts grass fast and picks 2 berries at a time, and wears out after 10 uses.
The stone axe now needs 1 twine too, to lash the head on.
The stone axe looks like an axe now: a flat stone head with a curved cutting edge, lashed on with twine.
Energy is now called Stamina, the berry bush button says Pick berries, and people away for over a day show 'away · fast asleep'.
The axe in your hand is turned round so the cutting edge faces the right way.
Running out of Rest no longer kills you. Your person collapses asleep where they stand, like in real life, and can't be woken until Rest is back to 25%.
Ready for more players: up to 20 can play at once. When the world is full you wait in line on the main menu and join by yourself when a spot opens.
Walking now sends far fewer messages to the server (where you're going, not every step), so the world stays inside Cloudflare's free plan.
The server saves less often while people just walk about (what you do is still saved straight away).
Your phone only draws the 30 people nearest you, so a busy world stays smooth.
Away for 48 hours and your person leaves the world (a day strolling, then a day asleep). Welcome back tells you how long you have.
Admin: the Admin panel shows today's server use against the free limit, and how many are playing and waiting.
New main menu: Play, What's new, Settings and Feedback, over a live view of the world slowly circling the main pond.
Under Play it shows who you'll carry on as, or that you'll make a new person.
Make your person has a Back button.
The pause menu is now just Resume and Exit (Exit goes back to the main menu and your person goes away and looks after themselves).
Graphics moved to Settings on the main menu.
Tidied up old code and the help notes for adding items.
The walking tip no longer covers your needs when you open them, the chat or the inventory.
Admin: the Feedback, reports, players list now opens in place of the Admin panel, and Close (or Escape) goes back to it.
Chopping: with a stone axe, tap a tree and Chop tree (about 10 s). You get a log and 2 sticks, and a stump is left.
Stumps grow back into trees after 3 days, unless you Remove stump (about 10 s, 1 more log): then the tree is gone for good. The old stumps already in the world can be dug out the same way.
Tap a log on the ground and Chop into sticks (about 8 s, 4 sticks). Logs weigh 10.
Each chop wears your axe (20 uses), and it breaks when worn out. Chopping takes a fair bit of energy.
A need under 10% flashes so you can't miss it.
New need: Rest (the moon ring, between health and hunger). Awake it lasts about 16 hours; sleeping fills it in about 8.

New need: Energy (the yellow ring on the right). Every task and walk takes a little; it comes back while you take it easy, and twice as fast asleep. Too low and your person needs a breather before doing more.
Realistic sleep: 8 hours fills Rest (about 12 an hour), and you get hungry and thirsty more slowly while asleep.
Tap yourself and choose Sleep; tap yourself again (or give your person something to do) to wake up. Others see you lying down, sleeping.
People who are away or on autopilot sleep by themselves when they get tired.
No rest for about 3 days and you collapse and die.
Sticks, stones, berries and the stone axe look better, each with a little variety, and show as small pictures in your Inventory and Craft.
The stone axe is held properly: by the end of the handle, head up, blade forward.
New look everywhere: dark glass panels, small round buttons, and your needs as rings (tap them for numbers).
Crafting: tap the hammer at the bottom to see what you can make and what you still need. First up, a stone axe from 2 sticks and 3 stones.
Your stone axe shows in your hand, with a wear bar in your inventory (20 uses). Chopping comes next.
Chat: Say opens a chat bar at the bottom with the last few messages. It stays open until you tap the world.
Walking finds a way round rocks, bushes, trees and the pond, for you and people who are away.
Close or switch away from the game and your person goes 'away' straight away and starts strolling about.
You can see what others are doing: bending to pick things up, picking berries, kneeling to drink (people who are away too).
Shorter menus: admin options sit behind one Admin item, a smaller Admin panel, and this list folds older updates.
Bug fixes: coming back puts you where your person strolled to.
Patch: the coloured flower dots on the ground are gone.
Patch: leave the game open without touching it for 3 minutes and your person goes on autopilot (eats, drinks, picks berries, strolls). Tap to take over.
Patch: people strolling while away walk round the pond, not through it.
Patch 3: people away (and on autopilot) stay within about 25 m of the pond.
Patch 3: name tags fade out behind the top and bottom bars, tap menus stay clear of them, and the Say box opens just under the top info.
Patch 4: the task list only shows while your person is doing something. Inventory and pop-ups sit above the bottom bars again.
Patch 5: walking finds a way round rocks, bushes, trees and the pond, so people don't get stuck (you, and people strolling while away).
Your person lives on the server and stays in the world while you're away.
Away: they stroll about, eat, pick berries and drink. After a day they sleep; after 7 days asleep they leave.
Welcome back card, 'away' and 'asleep' name tags, graves.
Realistic needs: hunger lasts a day, thirst about 16 hours. Berries fill 10, drinks fill 15.
26 more berry bushes. Tap the ground for Walk here. Say button at the bottom. What's new in the Menu.
Fresh start: everyone makes a new person.
Online: one shared world, other people, speech bubbles.
Online count, Graphics setting, Send feedback.
Chat filter, Mute and Report.
Double-tap to walk.
Berry bushes, tap menus, task list, pause menu.
Walking round rocks and trees. Saving.
